## Rule

Inputs are square lattices whose active widths are 8, 11, 14, 15, 17, 19, or 23. The output is the cell-color grid sampled from the lattice, horizontally flipped, then padded back to `[1,10,30,30]`.

Most widths map to either a 3x3 or 4x4 cell grid by width alone. Width 11 is ambiguous: it is 4x4 when row 2 contains a horizontal divider, detected cheaply by comparing color-index cells `(2,2)` and `(2,3)`; otherwise it is 3x3.

## Algorithm sketch

```python
w = active_square_width(input)

# Width-11 ambiguity: compare full one-hot vectors at row-2 cells.
use_11_4x4 = (w == 11) and dot(input[:, :, 2, 2], input[:, :, 2, 3]) == 1
rows, cols = table_by_width[w]
if use_11_4x4:
    rows, cols = [0, 3, 6, 9], [9, 6, 3, 0]

row_sel = one_hot(rows, depth=30)  # [4,30]
col_sel = one_hot(cols, depth=30)  # [4,30]
sampled = einsum(input, row_sel, col_sel, "bkrc,ir,jc->bkij")
output = pad(sampled, to_shape=[1, 10, 30, 30])
```

## 2026-07-07 ceiling audit (Claude bo_ng_cld_worker1) — TRUE BAR 85, WALL

**The Attempts table above and the AUTO STATUS (2,252 / 753) are STALE.** The authoritative live bar is
**cost 85** (`ng_current_bar.py --task 244 --json`: manifest, owner Vamshi, sha `db55e34c…`, updated 2026-07-02).
The live winner is NOT any local selector-Einsum prototype — it is a 6-node **RoiAlign** graph in
`Team_Best_Onnx/task244.onnx`, score `(macs=0, memory=44, params=41)`:

`Einsum(deg-11 width fingerprint r11) → Greater(thresholds[8]) → Cast(U8) → ArgMin(first-unpassed) → Gather(roi_table[8,1,4]) → RoiAlign(out 30×30, spatial_scale 1)`.
RoiAlign fuses sample+hflip+pad into one attr-only op; the `roi_table` ROI coords use `x2<x1` to encode the flip.

**Prompt "perfect-25 → cost 1" premise is FALSE.** The output geometry is width-dependent (widths
8/11/14/15/17/19/23 + the width-11 3×3-vs-4×4 branch = **8 distinct ROI cases**), so no payload-free single
op (Identity/Transpose/Flip) can produce it. A width discriminator (threshold vector) + a per-width geometry
table are both forced ⇒ cost ≫ 1. The live 85 graph is the existence proof of the minimal structural cost.

**Sub-85 shave attempted & failed** (`hard_records/reducesum_count_selector.md`): drop the `1e30` ArgMin
sentinel via `bucket = ReduceSum(r11 > thresholds[7])` (7 separators, exact same bucketing — visible 266/266).
ORT rejects `ReduceSum` on UINT8; INT32/INT64/FLOAT force a ≥4 B/elem width-K plane (`passed_i32[7]`=28 B),
which adds +20 B memory to save −1 param ⇒ **cost 99 > 85, LOSES**. Prototype
`prototypes/task244_reducesum7_roialign.onnx` (sha `e106e570…`).

**WALL at 85.** Every selector shave is closed (this record + `continuous_log_affine_roi.md`,
`log_quant_roi.md`, `low_level_selector_legality.md`). Forced components: `roi_table[8,1,4]`=32 params
(8 geometry cases × 4 coords), `rois[1,4]` f32=16 B (RoiAlign input), `Greater→Cast(u8)→ArgMin` selector
(u8 cast + int64 output forced by op type contracts), `thresholds[8]` (7 separators + 1 argmin sentinel),
`batch_idx[1]`. A sub-85 win requires **deleting a forced structural component** (table-free ROI generator, or
a cheaper op than RoiAlign for width-dependent flipped affine resample) — none known. No stage (no tie-or-below).

## Cost analysis

Old graph cost was 53897 in the current diagnostic (older live note: 55302), dominated by 10 Gather intermediates over one-hot channel tensors: [1,10,K,30] tensors total roughly 44 KB. Crop attempts only shaved around 1.4 KB because the branch selector still needed full-width information.

`task244_v1` cost was 4935 (memory=4631, params=304). The largest live tensor was the color-index canvas `[1,30,30]` at 3600B, which blocks any sub-3000 candidate.

`task244_v6` cost is 2252 (memory=2055, params=197). The largest counted tensors are `sampled_onehot` `[1,10,4,4]` at 640B, the two F32 selectors `row_sel`/`col_sel` `[4,30]` at 480B each, `col_mass` `[1,30]` at 120B, and the width-11 probe tensors at 80B/40B/40B. This is below 3000 while keeping a full 200k truth pass. A lower floor would need to eliminate or shrink the selector matrices; direct dynamic `GatherND` and pure-INT32 `OneHot` paths were rejected in this ORT/scorer setup.
